title: A blank page
summary: Labÿrínta begins as nothing at all: an empty page, the first room of a labyrinth not yet built.

title: The first carving
summary: The blank page becomes a lattice, and out of it a sentence is carved as a real maze in the grammar of the 'A Labyrinth Is a …' series: letters as white corridors, one way in at the top left, one way out at the bottom right.
details: A maze-letter alphabet and generator (site/maze.js): glyphs drawn as corridors on a five-row grid, joined by a random minimum spanning tree so every corridor is reachable and a route always exists
Line breaks chosen live for the screen, so the carving reflows from two lines on desktop to a stepped cascade on a phone
The carving animates: the lattice thickens into a template, then walls fall away in the order a flood from the entrance reaches them (static under reduced motion)
29 sentences: Luke Bradford's titles credited with venue and year, plus a few new ones marked as new; each has a shareable #address
Light and dark schemes, the ÿ's two sealed cells as favicon, and VISION.md written

title: Ariadne's thread
summary: Every carving can now be walked. A loose end of thread waits at the entrance; drag it through the corridors (or use the arrow keys), and leaving by the exit carves the next sentence. The four sentences of Four Paths lead into one another.
details: Pointer and touch dragging follow the corridors from the head of the thread; walking back winds the thread up, and walking into a loop cuts it off
Arrow keys walk the maze; the canvas is focusable and describes itself; the caption announces each new sentence politely
Exiting draws the thread out through the gap, then moves to the next sentence (the Four Paths cycle, otherwise a new one) with a history entry, so Back retraces your way
A phone toolbar sliding away no longer re-breaks the lines and loses the thread
The generator modules are imported with the page's version stamp, so returning visitors never mix old and new code

title: Only new sentences
summary: The owner's rule: his visual poems may appear only if published, and only as exact reproductions down to every wall segment. The site had been carving his titles in its own alphabet (approximate versions) and showing unpublished titles, so all of them are removed; the lattice now carves only sentences written new for Labÿrínta.
details: Removed all 23 sentences taken from Luke Bradford's maze poems (16 published titles carved approximately, 7 unpublished) and the Four Paths loop that walked through four of them
Fifteen new sentences, each marked new; five use only the letters of labyrinth
The rule is written into VISION.md and the sentence list so future sessions keep it
Fixed a layout bug where a wide carving on a short screen ran into the credit in the top left; the maze now steps down by whole rows to clear it, and shrinks if the caption would fall off screen

title: A rectangle with two gaps
summary: Every carving's edge is now a plain rectangle with one gap in at the top left and one out at the bottom right, as in the series. Before, short lines left indents in the frame and dead lattice cells inside it.
details: Short lines are justified: their spare columns become small open word spaces, toned like the other non-letter corridors, shared between the gaps and the line ends
The layout avoids wide word spaces, so lines break where the spaces stay narrow
Checked across 75 carvings (every sentence at five screen sizes): full rectangle, no dead cells, every corridor reachable, a route from entrance to exit

title: The published poems, exactly
summary: The site now shows only Luke Bradford's published maze poems, read stroke by stroke from the published PDFs and verified pixel for pixel, with the carving, Ariadne's thread and the walk from poem to poem. The generated sentences and the site's own alphabet are gone.
details: Fifteen rooms, one per published page, in order of publication: Four Paths (i–iv), Four Paths II (i–iv), Two Paths, A Labyrinth Is a Barrel of Laughs, Mesh, A Labyrinth Is a Narrow Hell, A Labyrinth Is a Borderline, Language Is a Trap, One Path; each credited with venue and date

site/poems.js holds every wall stroke as published (endpoints within 0.0002 pt of the PDFs); tools/poems/extract.py regenerates it and tools/poems/verify.py checks it, including a headless-Chrome check that the site's canvas matches MuPDF renders of the PDFs with zero differing pixels
Walking is read off the published walls (site/walls.js): Two Paths is walked maze by maze, and Language Is a Trap has no way out, as published
Removed the maze-letter generator, the invented sentences and the ÿ favicon; the page is light only, like the poems

title: Three more, found online
summary: A Labyrinth Is a Library of Babel, A Labyrinth Is a Rabbit Hole and A Labyrinth Is Barely Real join the walk. They were published only as images, so each is drawn from the author's vector file after checking it wall by wall against the published image.
details: Library of Babel (petrichor, April 2019) and Rabbit Hole (The Blasted Tree broadside, 2019) come after Two Paths; Barely Real (The Minute Review 2.4, May 2022) comes before Language Is a Trap: 18 rooms in all

tools/poems/verify.py gains a fourth check: the wall on every cell edge of each published image (petrichor's PNG, The Blasted Tree's PNG, The Minute Review's scan) matches the vector, and every differing pixel lies on a stroke's edge; Rabbit Hole's renders to the published PNG with no differing pixels
The site's canvas still matches MuPDF renders of the sources with zero differing pixels in every room

title: Grey before ink
summary: The walls no longer start thin and swell to their width as the template darkens. They stand at full width from the first frame, in the grey of the lattice, and darken to ink in one smooth gradient that sweeps across the maze.
details: Template edges and poem walls are drawn at their final stroke width throughout the opening animation
Their colour comes from a diagonal canvas gradient, lattice grey to ink, with a soft front moving from top left to bottom right
Settled poems are unchanged, pixel for pixel

title: Out of white
summary: The full-width walls no longer appear all at once when a room opens: they fade up from white to the grey of the lattice, then darken to ink in the same diagonal sweep.
details: Wall colour rises from white over the first 350 ms, blending into the grey-to-ink gradient
Settled poems are unchanged, pixel for pixel
